question: What best describes disease surveillance in public health practice?

options.A: Treatment of individual patients in hospital wards
options.B: An ongoing and systematic collection of health data
options.C: A one-time survey conducted during a major crisis
options.D: Laboratory testing of water samples in urban areas

explanation: Surveillance requires continuous monitoring and data collection rather than isolated assessments to track health trends over time. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h1)

question: Why is disease surveillance described as an early warning system?

options.A: It predicts exact weather patterns causing malaria outbreaks
options.B: It tells nurses when patients will be discharged from wards
options.C: It alerts authorities to unusual increases in illness early
options.D: It stops patients from visiting crowded outpatient clinics

explanation: Continuous tracking allows health teams to detect spikes in disease incidence before they escalate into major outbreaks. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h1)

question: A major objective of public health surveillance is to...

options.A: Schedule annual leave for ministry health workers
options.B: Manage administrative promotions within nursing units
options.C: Detect epidemics early to mount a rapid response
options.D: Provide personal loans for private hospital owners

explanation: Early identification of disease spikes allows health agencies to deploy interventions quickly and contain spread. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h2)

question: How does surveillance data assist health ministries in resource management?

options.A: By guiding where to distribute vaccines and medical personnel
options.B: By setting the admission fees for undergraduate students
options.C: By determining the monthly salaries of clinical nursing staff
options.D: By calculating the electricity bills of government hospitals

explanation: Accurate tracking shows where disease burdens are highest, ensuring supplies and staff go where they are needed most. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h2)

question: Which surveillance system relies on healthcare workers sending routine reports without prompting?
explanation: Passive surveillance involves routine reporting from facilities where staff initiate the transmission of health data. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h3)

question: When is active surveillance most appropriate to implement in a health district?

options.A: To monitor general long-term chronic illness trends nationwide
options.B: For routine daily collection of outpatient clinic attendance logs
options.C: During an ongoing disease outbreak requiring intensive case finding
options.D: When tracking overall school absenteeism rates during dry seasons

explanation: Active surveillance requires visiting facilities and searching records, which is resource-intensive and best used during investigations. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h3)

question: What is the immediate step following data collection in the surveillance cycle?

options.A: Immediate discharge of all reporting patients
options.C: Data transmission up the reporting hierarchy
options.D: Destruction of physical paper record books

explanation: Once health data is collected at the facility level, it must be transmitted upward to local and national authorities. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h4)

question: Why is analyzing data by time, place, and person essential in surveillance?

options.A: It ensures hospital administrators receive higher funding
options.B: It calculates the exact budget for nursing uniforms
options.C: It helps identify patterns and pinpoint outbreak sources
options.D: It replaces the need for clinical laboratory testing

explanation: Breaking down data by these three epidemiological variables reveals where and among whom an illness is spreading. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h4)

question: What does IDSR stand for in the context of Nigerian public health?
explanation: IDSR is the standardized strategy adopted across African nations to harmonize surveillance and response activities. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard data source within the IDSR framework?
explanation: Financial portfolios have no bearing on health tracking, whereas clinic logs, laboratory results, and community reports form the bedrock of surveillance data. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of establishing a case definition during an outbreak investigation?

options.A: To calculate the monthly budget for hospital medications
options.B: To determine nursing shift schedules in the ward
options.C: To evaluate the academic performance of medical interns
options.D: To consistently identify who is affected by the disease

explanation: A clear case definition ensures that all team members use the same clinical and epidemiological criteria to count cases accurately. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h6)

question: Why must control measures be implemented while an outbreak investigation is still ongoing?

options.A: To halt further transmission and prevent more infections
options.B: To allow researchers to close their offices early
options.C: To stop patients from seeking care at private clinics
options.D: To fulfill paperwork requirements for international donors

explanation: Waiting for a complete scientific report before intervening would allow the disease to spread unchecked through the population. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h6)

question: Why are clinical nurses considered frontline workers in disease surveillance?

options.A: They are usually the first to assess and care for sick individuals
options.B: They hold administrative management positions in federal ministries
options.C: They handle international funding logistics for health programs
options.D: They are exclusively responsible for laboratory PCR testing

explanation: Patients present to nurses first in clinics and wards, making the nurse the primary observer of initial symptoms. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h7)

question: What is a key responsibility of a community health nurse regarding surveillance outside the hospital?

options.A: Purchasing medical equipment from international manufacturing firms
options.B: Drafting national legislative bills for health sector reform
options.C: Educating households and monitoring for unusual illness clusters
options.D: Auditing financial statements of private pharmaceutical suppliers

explanation: Community nurses bridge the gap between formal health systems and local populations by spotting trends and educating the public. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h7)

question: A major operational challenge facing traditional surveillance systems in Nigeria is...

options.A: Excessive funding resulting in inflated administrative budgets
options.B: Too many reference laboratories performing rapid diagnostics
options.C: Underreporting due to heavy workloads and paper form stockouts
options.D: An overwhelming surplus of digital tablets in rural clinics

explanation: Busy schedules and a lack of reporting supplies often cause healthcare workers to miss or delay submitting disease reports. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h8)

question: What is the primary benefit of transitioning to electronic IDSR (e-IDSR) systems?

options.A: Lowering the cost of hospital building construction projects
options.B: Enabling real-time data transmission and bypassing paper delays
options.C: Reducing the total number of patients seeking outpatient care
options.D: Eliminating the need for any clinical staff in health facilities

explanation: Digital tools speed up reporting pathways, allowing authorities to view and act on surveillance data instantly. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h8)
